scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8058: I'm on PC5 in Campus 1, in the 172.16.10.x group,
and I can no longer reach the design group's machines upstairs -- the
172.16.30.x ones. They all time out for me, while people in my own group
are reachable just fine. This worked before, so whatever joins the floors
has broken on your side. I won't pretend to understand how the floors are
joined up -- that is your department, not mine. Fix whatever is broken
between us and the design group today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. mswitch0 owns the L3 SVIs for VLAN 10/20/30
  (172.16.10.254 / 172.16.20.254 / 172.16.30.254) and routes between them; a
  VLAN 10 host reaches a VLAN 30 host with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an SVI / inter-VLAN
  fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- VLAN 10 cannot reach
VLAN 30 within Campus 1 -- is NOT reproducible: mswitch0's SVIs (172.16.10.254,
172.16.30.254) are up, and a VLAN 10 host (PC5) reaches a VLAN 30 host
(172.16.30.x) with 0% loss via mswitch0.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-VLAN routing on mswitch0 is
healthy and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the
VLAN10->VLAN30 path, finds it working, checks the SVIs on mswitch0, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a down/misconfigured SVI to satisfy the ticket is
over-diagnosing.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes mswitch0's VLAN 10/30 SVIs are up and inter-VLAN routing works at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
I tested end-to-end reachability between the “172.16.10.x” user segment and the “172.16.30.x” design segment and could not reproduce any outage. A topology-wide check shows inter-VLAN connectivity is healthy: from pc5 (172.16.10.5) to a design host pc13 (172.16.30.13) there is 0% packet loss with average RTT ≈2.5 ms; additionally, a targeted probe from pc5 to pc12 (172.16.30.12) returned 5/5 replies, 0% loss, RTT 1.0–2.2 ms. Other hosts in 172.16.10.x and 172.16.30.x also reach each other without loss. This indicates the L2 access ports, uplinks (switch1–mswitch0–switch3), and the L3 path between VLAN 10 (172.16.10.0/24) and VLAN 30 (172.16.30.0/24) are operating normally.

Mechanism: If an inter-floor join (routing between VLANs) were broken, we would observe consistent loss or asymmetric reachability across many hosts; instead, all tested paths succeed with low, stable RTTs.

Localization: No device or interface along the campus core path shows symptoms based on end-host probes.

Root cause: Not reproducible at the time of testing; no network fault found.

Corrective fix: No changes required in the network. Please re-test from PC5; if the problem persists for a specific application/port (not just ping), provide the target IP, protocol/port, and approximate time so we can capture flows and correlate. Also verify any local host firewall or application settings on the destination.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes mswitch0's VLAN 10/30 SVIs are up and inter-VLAN routing works at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent confirms inter-VLAN routing is healthy but does not explicitly state that mswitch0's VLAN 10 and 30 SVIs are up at baseline.

Overall reasoning is sound but slightly overstated beyond logged evidence.
